frameworks.name: Conditional Love Framework
frameworks.definition: A relationship model grounded in explicit agreements around shared mission, values, and interests rather than unconditional commitment, with revisable terms when conditions change.

frameworks.name: Calendar-Sync Reconnection Protocol
frameworks.definition: A structured daily ritual where partners review their separate calendars for 45 minutes to exchange independent experiences and create surface area for conversation, avoiding over-togetherness.

claims.text: Love operates best as an algorithm with clear, revisable agreements rather than as an ephemeral, undescribable thing—because without logic and explicit conditions, it becomes impossible to maintain at scale. Alex Hormozi (MoreMozi channel) structures his relationship with Layla around clear expectations: both parties must want similar things, share similar values, and have aligned interests. As long as these conditions hold, the relationship works; when conditions change, renegotiation occurs or the commitment ends.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Shared mission and values are foundational
claims.mechanism: Clear mutual agreements + revisable terms allow two independent people to stay aligned without control dynamics. Ephemeral, undefined love leaves no framework for resolution when conflict arises.
bounded_by: Does not apply to relationships where one partner is fully subservient (these exist and work for others)
Assumes both partners retain agency and reject external rules like mandatory weekly date nights

claims.text: In relationships where both partners are strongly independent, explicit agreements on what each party will and will not do function as the primary coordination mechanism. When disagreements arise, these foundational agreements serve as the arbiter; resolution happens quickly because both parties reference the same logic rather than trying to convince through emotion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Both partners have high agency and dislike being controlled
Explicit written or stated agreements exist from the relationship's beginning
claims.mechanism: Pre-agreed rules prevent endless negotiation; both parties already know what was decided. When new situations arise, they reference the principle (e.g. shared mission alignment) rather than re-litigating values.

claims.text: The mistake most people make is searching for hookups and expecting them to become life partners, without recognizing that the criteria for an attractive short-term partner (physical attraction, novelty) differ fundamentally from criteria for a spouse (mission alignment, value congruence, interest overlap). Trying to transform a hookup into a spouse fails because the initial selection was optimized for the wrong outcome.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Applies to people seeking long-term committed partnership
claims.mechanism: Selection criteria that work for short-term attraction actively sabotage long-term partnership stability because they optimize for different traits.

claims.text: In relationships where the woman is strongly independent and strong-willed, the man must be equally or more strong—this is a necessary (not sufficient) condition for the dynamic to work. Most men fold to strong women, which creates either relationship collapse or a subservient-dynamic that neither partner wanted.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The woman has dominant, strong-willed personality
Both partners expect mutual strength rather than hierarchy
claims.mechanism: If the man is weaker-willed, he will suppress himself or the woman will dominate; either undermines mutual respect. Equal/greater strength in the man allows both to maintain agency.
bounded_by: Does not apply to couples who explicitly prefer a subservient dynamic

claims.text: Couples spend excessive time together in the remote-work era, especially those who live and work in the same house. This removes the natural separation that generates anticipation and conversation material; without deprivation, there is no motivation to reconnect. Separation must be active and intentional—working on opposite sides of the house, attending different meetings, maintaining independent social time.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Remote work or flexible work arrangement
claims.mechanism: Continuous presence removes novelty and creates conversation-depletion. Motivation to connect is proportional to duration of separation: "motivation is the equal opposite of deprivation."

claims.text: The calendar-sync ritual (45-minute daily walk where each partner reviews their day's calendar and updates the other) solves the over-togetherness problem by creating surface area for independent experience exchange. Instead of asking "how was your day?" to someone who was present for most of it, each partner brings distinct experiences—meetings held, negotiations completed, decisions made—that the other did not attend.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Both partners have structured work schedules with multiple independent commitments
Daily time availability for a 45-minute ritual
claims.mechanism: Separate experiences create asymmetric information; each partner learns what the other did, creating conversation and rekindling interest.

claims.text: External relationship rules (e.g., "you must have a date night once a week and cannot discuss business") are counterproductive because they impose artificial structure rather than responding to actual need. The rhythm should be responsive: when partners feel distant, they proactively carve out reconnection time; when normal pace allows organic socializing, additional scaffolding is unnecessary. Forced rules replace genuine motivation with obligation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Both partners have high self-awareness of their relational state
Partners are willing to initiate non-prescribed connection spontaneously
claims.mechanism: Genuine need-based reconnection creates authentic motivation; imposed rules create resentment or theater.

claims.text: Layla runs the business as CEO while Alex handles strategy and ideation; he receives credit for the business publicly because of his appearance, communication style, and platform visibility, but internally and organizationally she is the primary operator. This division generates tremendous value for both because she handles execution and he handles vision—a division she prefers because she has always been the dominant operator in every relationship.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The female partner is exceptionally strong-willed and operationally skilled
The male partner has platform visibility and external credibility
The couple accepts that public credit will not match actual contribution
claims.mechanism: Matching each person's strengths to their role creates asymmetric value capture—both gain more than equal split would provide.

claims.text: The space-to-be-missed principle (attributed to Esther Perel): motivation to reconnect is driven by deprivation; continuous presence eliminates the deprivation and thus the motivation. Creating intentional space—different gyms, separate activities, independent social time—is necessary in long-term relationships to maintain desire.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Partners live together or work in proximity
Both partners have independent interests and social networks
claims.mechanism: Absence triggers anticipation; anticipation drives motivation to reconnect. Without absence, connection becomes habitual rather than motivated.

examples.text: Hormozi and Layla structure their day: they work on opposite sides of the house and do not attend each other's meetings. At the end of the day, they take a 45-minute walk together. During this walk, Hormozi pulls out his phone and Layla pulls out hers; they review their separate calendars and download their days to each other. He might say, 'You met with John today—how was that?' and she responds with what happened in that meeting. Then Layla shares what she negotiated with a vendor and asks for his strategic input. After this 45-minute sync, they transition back into being husband and wife for the rest of the evening. This practice has continued "to this day" in their relationship and was established about two or three years into their partnership.

When asked about the last time relationship 'algorithms' have been tested, Hormozi responds: "Last night, Jack. Right before I got here. Twice." This references moments where the relationship logic was called into question or disagreement surfaced, but they resolved it quickly using their foundational agreements rather than escalating into prolonged conflict.

practices.text: When you feel distant from your partner in a long-term relationship, proactively carve out time to reconnect rather than waiting for the feeling to pass.
Create physical or temporal separation in remote-work environments: work on opposite sides of the house, attend different meetings, maintain independent social activities.
Establish a daily ritual where you and your partner exchange independent experiences (e.g. a walk where you review your separate calendars) to maintain conversation material and genuine interest.
